title: Nvidia Can't Buy Enough of It. I Found 2 Ways In
summary: Brian argues memory — not electricity, as Elon Musk claims — is the true scarce input in the AI buildout, evidenced by Nvidia's gross margin slipping to 75% (guided to 72-73%) as COGS doubled to $63B, and its 'supply and capacity' commitments footnote jumping from $119B to $279B, primarily for memory and manufacturing. His method: compare each company's last four quarters of gross margin against the prior four — margin only rises when you own something scarce. Across 24 companies tested, 13 passed. Vertiv passes (+4.3 points on +26% revenue, deferred revenue doubling to $3.6B) but gains little pricing power; nVent fails (margin -2.2 points on +46% revenue — a commodity). SanDisk, spun from Western Digital 18 months ago, is the cleanest pass: gross margin from 26% to 85%, +41.4 points with revenue nearly tripling. Micron is the headline: same-quarter margin from 37.7% to 84.6% (+35.4 points), ~6x next-year earnings, with 16 long-term supply agreements to 2030 and customers getting only 50-67% of requested supply — though the market may be pricing a repeat of the 2018 peak-to-bust cycle. The real risk is China: a state-backed memory maker's $8.6B July IPO, now starting ~9 wafers for every 10 Micron starts, with Apple testing its chips and US senators pushing back. Constellation Energy (+24.5 points) is the honest electricity trade (already-built, licensed reactors), but he hasn't done valuation work on it — not a recommendation. Calls: SNDK BUY; MU BUY; VTI UNCERTAIN; NVT AVOID; CEG UNCERTAIN. Sponsored segment for CopperOne Resources.
